source_text: non innovari homines per Baptismum, sed quasi innovari; non liberari, sed quasi liberari; non salvari, sed quasi salvari
pass_a_gloss: Not innovari human-beings through Baptismum, but as-if innovari; not liberari, but as-if liberari; not salvari, but as-if salvari.
pass_b_english: People are not renewed through baptism, but only supposedly renewed; not freed, but only supposedly freed; not saved, but only supposedly saved.
Augustine reports that Julian compares this position to Epicurus’s teaching that the gods have not a body but something like a body, not blood but something like blood.
Whatever is done in the present age deserves blame.

choices.why: Keep the rite-name; Julian says praise of baptism is being used to smuggle natural evil.
Freedom to abstain is required for will and sin.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
kind: Julian allegations and an authority he invokes
